concepts.name: Evolution
concepts.short_description: Descent with modification via natural selection; fitness landscapes, speciation, genetic drift.

concepts.name: Phenomenology
concepts.short_description: First-person study of conscious experience and its structures; intentionality, bracketing, lifeworld.

concepts.name: Reservoir Computing
concepts.short_description: Fixed random recurrent network with trainable readout; echo state networks, liquid state machines.

unexplained: whether any interpretation needs phenomenology causally rather than as vocabulary
no reproduction notion in phenomenology or reservoir computing; evolution supplies all of it

selection acts on phenotype, inheritance passes genotype
no foresight: variation is blind to future fitness
conserved_quantities: none conserved in the genotype itself
failure_modes: error catastrophe above a mutation threshold
drift fixing deleterious variants in small populations
dynamics: Red Queen / tracking of moving optima

sediment of historical contingency in lineage

information: genome accumulates information about environment at rate bounded by selection strength

time-consciousness triad: retention / primal impression / protention
invariants: the intentional object is identical across varying acts (noematic invariance under adumbrations)
the living present always has retentional and protentional fringes
constitution is layered: passive synthesis precedes active judgment
transformations: epoche (bracketing: suspension of the natural attitude, not deletion)
eidetic variation (vary an example imaginatively to find what cannot change)
sedimentation (active achievements become passive habitual background)
conserved_quantities: identity of the noema across profiles
failure_modes: naturalistic objectification (treating experience as just another thing)
sedimented background becomes invisible and uncorrectable
dynamics: continuous flow of the living present sinking into retention
locality: the here of the lived body
the now of the living present

identity: identity of an object = invariant through a manifold of appearances
identity of the ego as pole of acts

constraint: one can only intend what the horizon makes available

defining_structures: fixed (random) recurrent dynamical system driven by input
invariants: echo state property: state is asymptotically a function of input history only, independent of initial condition
transformations: nonlinear expansion of input history into high-dimensional state
linear regression from state to target
hyperparameter changes (spectral radius, leak, input scale, sparsity)
conserved_quantities: total linear memory capacity bounded by state dimension N
failure_modes: chaotic regime: loss of echo state property, sensitivity to initial state
dynamics: operation near the edge of stability
scales: memory horizon set by spectral radius and leak rate
locality: temporal locality: recent inputs dominate state
memory: no memory in the readout beyond weights
identity: a reservoir is identified by its weight matrix; readouts are only meaningful relative to one reservoir
selection: readout training selects a linear functional of state; hyperparameter search selects reservoirs
constraint: only linear functionals of state are decodable
readout cannot recover what the state has forgotten

unexplained: M1, M11, M12 have weak phenomenology dependency and may be ordinary search
whether sedimentation (M3) differs from Lamarckian readout inheritance
whether richness (M4) is more than effective rank
no lens yet separates embodiment (M13) from generic physical reservoirs
all worlds are ESN populations; no cross-substrate world yet (mass-spring M13 is a candidate)
M5, M10, M14 have no world

hypotheses.statement: The reservoir's fading memory is a specious present (retention + protention fringes around the input now). Evolution does not select what is known but how wide the living present is: heritable leak rate and spectral radius are selected to match the temporal structure of the environment, and the retention/protention balance is itself an evolved trait.

The reservoir/readout split is an epoche: the fixed dynamics are the bracketed background that is not modified in life, while the readout is the active attitude learned in life. Evolution then acts on the bracketed layer only, producing a Baldwin-style division of labour between heritable fixed dynamics and lifetime-trained readouts.

The reservoir is not random but a sediment of ancestral readouts: across generations, readouts that were learned actively are compiled back into fixed recurrent dynamics (sedimentation / genetic assimilation), so the 'random' reservoir of a lineage carries a stratigraphy of past tasks that makes their relearning cheap.

Intentionality as readout multiplicity: one state stream supports many intentional objects via many readouts. Evolution can select reservoirs for noematic richness (how many distinct target functionals are linearly decodable) rather than for any single task, yielding reservoirs that transfer to unseen tasks.

Lifeworld incommensurability as speciation: a readout is meaningful only relative to its reservoir, so readouts cannot be exchanged between divergent reservoirs. Readout-transplant failure is a reproductive-isolation criterion, and species are sets of individuals sharing a horizon of decodability.

Epoche as an evolved input gate: when readout capacity is limited, lineages that suspend (mask) distracting input channels without losing them from the world gain fitness; bracketing is a heritable, selected information bottleneck rather than a method.

Noema as invariant across reservoirs: if the readout is heritable but each individual's reservoir is freshly resampled in development, only readouts addressing properties invariant across reservoir realizations survive; evolution performs an eidetic variation over reservoirs and finds their invariant.
Horizon tuning: leak rate and spectral radius are heritable; fitness is lifetime readout error on a task with characteristic delay D; the population's memory-capacity profile migrates to centre on D.

concept_contributions.Evolution: heritable variation and selection on reservoir hyperparameters
concept_contributions.Phenomenology: the framing of memory width as a specious present (weak: no causal role)
concept_contributions.Reservoir Computing: fading memory whose width depends on hyperparameters

knockouts.Evolution: no adaptation of horizon; horizon stays at initial random value
knockouts.Phenomenology: nothing measurable disappears; phenomenology is decorative here (three-way dependency WEAK)

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Plain hyperparameter search (grid or random) over spectral radius and leak.

questions.what_exists: population of ESNs with heritable (rho, leak)
questions.what_can_transfer: horizon value to new tasks with same delay
questions.distinguishing_observable: memory-capacity peak lag tracks D across environments; must beat random search at equal evaluations to be more than search

hypotheses.statement: Bracketed inheritance: reservoir weights are heritable and never changed in life; readout is re-learned from scratch each life with a fixed small sample budget. Low lifetime budget pushes task information into the heritable reservoir; high budget leaves reservoir near-random.

concept_contributions.Phenomenology: the partition between bracketed (fixed) and active (learned) layers

knockouts.Evolution: reservoir stays random; all adaptation in readout
knockouts.Phenomenology: without the partition (everything trained in life) no division of labour exists to measure
knockouts.Reservoir Computing: no fixed layer to carry heredity

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Baldwin effect in any two-timescale learner (evolved init + fine-tuning).

questions.what_changes: reservoir weights across generations; readout within life
questions.what_is_selected: reservoirs whose readouts learn fast with few samples
questions.distinguishing_observable: task-relevant information in reservoir (ablation) as a decreasing function of lifetime sample budget

hypotheses.statement: Sedimentation operator: with probability p per birth, the parent's learned readout w is compiled into the offspring reservoir as a fixed feedback loop W <- W + eps * v w^T (v a random input-like vector). Actively learned functionals become passive background dynamics of descendants.

concept_contributions.Evolution: inheritance and selection that retain useful sediment
concept_contributions.Phenomenology: sedimentation: active achievement becomes passive habitual background
concept_contributions.Reservoir Computing: a fixed recurrent matrix into which a linear functional can be folded

knockouts.Evolution: sediment accumulates without filtering; noise dominates
knockouts.Phenomenology: operator becomes an ordinary random rank-one mutation
knockouts.Reservoir Computing: no fixed layer to deposit into

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Lamarckian inheritance of any learned parameter; or simply initializing offspring readout from parent readout.

questions.what_is_selected: lineages whose sediment helps current task
questions.what_can_transfer: fast relearning of ancestral task after task switch
questions.distinguishing_observable: few-shot relearning of an abandoned task beats a norm-matched random-deposit twin

hypotheses.statement: Noematic richness selection: fitness counts how many of K random target functionals of input history are linearly decodable above threshold, not performance on one task. Predicts better transfer to held-out functionals than task-selected reservoirs.

concept_contributions.Phenomenology: one stream, many intentional objects; fitness defined by readout multiplicity
concept_contributions.Reservoir Computing: linear decodability as the test of what is present in the state

knockouts.Evolution: reservoir stays random; no richness gain
knockouts.Phenomenology: fitness reverts to single-task; transfer advantage should vanish

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Selecting for high effective rank / memory capacity of the state covariance (a known reservoir quality metric).

questions.what_exists: reservoirs and a bank of random target functionals
questions.distinguishing_observable: held-out functional R^2 higher than both task-selected and effective-rank-selected reservoirs

hypotheses.statement: Readout-transplant speciation: mating succeeds only if parent A's readout, applied to parent B's reservoir, achieves error below a threshold. Compatibility classes (shared horizons) become species; isolation emerges where reservoirs diverge in decodable geometry.

concept_contributions.Phenomenology: horizons of mutual understanding define community membership
concept_contributions.Reservoir Computing: readouts only meaningful relative to a reservoir

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Assortative mating by genetic distance threshold.

questions.distinguishing_observable: transplant-compatibility graph modular even at matched weight-distance; transplant success not predicted by raw weight distance

hypotheses.statement: Retention/protention split: state decomposes into subspaces predictive of past inputs (retention) and of future inputs (protention); in environments with learnable regularity, selection shifts capacity from retention toward protention, with total bounded by N.

concept_contributions.Phenomenology: the two-sided structure of the living present

knockouts.Phenomenology: only past-memory capacity would be measured; the future side has no motivation (moderate dependency)

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Trained predictor; any predictive coding system shifts toward prediction when future is predictable.

questions.distinguishing_observable: future-capacity FC(k) rises while past MC(k) falls, sum bounded

hypotheses.statement: Epoche gate: heritable binary mask over input channels; readout limited to k taps. When k is small, evolution brackets high-variance uninformative channels (keeps them in the world, suspends them from the reservoir); when readout is unconstrained, masking is not selected.

concept_contributions.Reservoir Computing: limited readout makes distractor contamination costly

knockouts.Phenomenology: reduces to feature selection (knockout shows weak dependency)

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Feature selection by any wrapper method.

questions.what_can_transfer: mask to new task sharing distractors
questions.distinguishing_observable: masking of distractors depends on readout budget k (interaction), not merely on distractor presence

hypotheses.statement: Passive synthesis: during life, before readout training, the reservoir undergoes slow unsupervised intrinsic plasticity (gain/bias homeostasis) driven only by input exposure; the plasticity rate is heritable. Pre-reflective shaping precedes active readout.

concept_contributions.Reservoir Computing: a substrate whose gains can adapt

questions.what_changes: gains in life, rate across generations
questions.distinguishing_observable: evolved plasticity rate correlates with environmental nonstationarity

hypotheses.statement: Echo-state heredity boundary: because the echo state property erases initial conditions, environmental regularities with period longer than the reservoir horizon cannot be carried in state and must be carried genetically. Predicts a gap: structure at timescales below horizon is learned, above horizon is inherited or absent.

concept_contributions.Phenomenology: horizon as the limit of the living present

knockouts.Phenomenology: boundary exists but framing loses its motivation

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Any finite-memory learner needs slow parameters for slow structure.

questions.what_exists: reservoirs in environments with multiple periods
questions.what_can_transfer: slow-context encoding to environments sharing the slow period
questions.distinguishing_observable: ablation shows fast periods lost on readout reset, slow periods lost on reservoir randomization

hypotheses.statement: Lifeworld commons: one reservoir is shared by the whole population; individuals are only readouts. Individuals' outputs are fed back as reservoir input and the shared reservoir drifts under cumulative feedback, so readouts evolve against a world they collectively shape.

knockouts.Phenomenology: reduces to multi-agent control on a shared dynamical system

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Niche construction / multi-agent learning in a shared environment.

questions.what_changes: readouts and the reservoir's effective input
questions.distinguishing_observable: newcomer readouts learn faster in a commons shaped by an evolved population than in one shaped by random readouts

hypotheses.statement: Edge drift: under mutation plus selection on robustness of offspring fitness, spectral radius drifts toward the stability boundary because mutational robustness of readout performance peaks there; phenomenologically, horizon widens until it becomes unstable.
hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Selection for memory capacity pushes rho to 1 regardless of robustness.

questions.what_can_transfer: robust rho to new tasks of similar delay
questions.distinguishing_observable: rho distribution under robustness-only selection vs capacity-only selection

hypotheses.statement: Protention-fulfilment fitness: fitness is the rate of fulfilled vs disappointed anticipations (sign agreement of predicted and actual next input change), not squared error; predicts selection for reservoirs that anticipate qualitative events rather than magnitudes.

concept_contributions.Phenomenology: fulfilment/disappointment of protention as the unit

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Classification loss on sign of next change.

questions.distinguishing_observable: difference between reservoirs selected on sign-fulfilment and on MSE at matched MSE

hypotheses.statement: Embodied reservoir: the reservoir is a mass-spring body whose morphology is heritable; the body computes by being perturbed by the world, and only a linear readout of spring lengths is learned. The lived body is the zero-point of computation.

concept_contributions.Phenomenology: embodiment: the body as the medium of experience

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Morphological computation with random bodies plus trained readout.

questions.distinguishing_observable: evolved bodies beat random bodies at matched spring count and energy

hypotheses.statement: Eidetic variation over reservoirs: the readout is heritable but each individual's reservoir is resampled at birth from a heritable distribution. Selection keeps only readouts addressing reservoir-invariant properties (e.g., permutation-invariant aggregates), and the distribution evolves to make more properties invariant.

concept_contributions.Phenomenology: noema as what stays identical across varying acts; eidetic variation

knockouts.Phenomenology: the move from 'fixed reservoir' to 'ensemble' loses its reason (moderate)

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Readout converges to mean-field / population average, a trivial invariant.

questions.what_can_transfer: readout to any sample of the distribution
questions.distinguishing_observable: fraction of readout weight outside the trivial all-ones direction that remains useful across resamples

hypotheses.statement: Adumbration voting: several small reservoirs each receive a partial profile (subset of channels); a population-level readout reconciles them. Evolution selects channel-to-reservoir assignments; the object is only decodable jointly.

concept_contributions.Phenomenology: adumbrations: partial profiles jointly give the object

questions.distinguishing_observable: robustness to channel loss exceeds random assignment at equal overlap

lenses.name: Specious-present profile
lenses.rationale: Makes retention and protention jointly measurable as two capacity curves around the input now.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: reservoir state trajectory X(t) driven by input u(t)
lenses.transformation: for each lag k in [-20, 20], fit ridge readout from X(t) to u(t-k) on held-out data; record R^2 as MC(k) for k>0 and FC(k) for k<0
predictedSignals: centroid tracks environment delay under M1
FC rises and MC falls under M6 with sum bounded by N
lenses.nullExpectation: random reservoirs with same rho/leak give same profiles as evolved ones
failureModes: FC nonzero only because input is autocorrelated
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: Two-sided temporal capacity rather than single-task error.

lenses.name: Bracketing ledger
lenses.rationale: Locates where task information lives: heritable reservoir or lifetime readout.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: individual = (reservoir W, readout w) at end of life
lenses.transformation: two ablations: (a) reset readout and retrain with n samples; (b) replace W by a random reservoir with matched spectrum and retrain readout with same n; information attributed to reservoir = error(b) - error(a)
observables: gain as function of lifetime budget n
predictedSignals: reservoir gain decreases as n increases (M2)
lenses.nullExpectation: gain ~ 0 for all n in drift populations
failureModes: matched-spectrum replacement not matched in other statistics
readout noise dominates at small n
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: Attribution of competence to layer rather than total performance.

lenses.name: Horizon-fusion transplant matrix
lenses.rationale: Species as sets that share decodability, not genome similarity.
lenses.transformation: matrix T_ij = NRMSE of readout w_i applied to states of W_j; threshold into graph; compute Newman modularity; compare to weight-distance graph at same edge density
observables: rank correlation of T with weight distance
lenses.nullExpectation: T fully predicted by weight distance
failureModes: any divergence kills transplant, giving trivial all-incompatible graph
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: Relational compatibility structure of the population.

lenses.name: Sediment stratigraphy
lenses.rationale: Reads a lineage's reservoir as layered deposits of ancestral tasks.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: lineage reservoirs and the record of tasks faced by ancestors
lenses.transformation: for each ancestral task epoch, few-shot relearning error of that task from the current reservoir, relative to a norm-matched random-deposit twin; plot against age of epoch
observables: decay of advantage with epoch age
failureModes: deposit norm changes rho and memory generally, not task content

lenses.name: Noematic invariance under resampling
lenses.rationale: Tests which decodings survive changes of the act (reservoir) while the object (input history) is fixed.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: readout w and a family of reservoirs sampled from a distribution
lenses.transformation: evaluate w across 20 resampled reservoirs; decompose w into all-ones component and remainder; measure performance of each component across resamples
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: Separates trivial from non-trivial ensemble invariants.

lenses.name: Decodable-object census
lenses.rationale: Counts intentional objects a state stream supports.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: reservoir states on a fixed input stream
lenses.transformation: fit readouts to K=40 random functionals (random degree-2 polynomials of last 10 inputs); count R^2 > 0.5; split 20 train/20 held-out
predictedSignals: held-out R^2 rises beyond what effective rank predicts (M4)
lenses.nullExpectation: held-out R^2 is a function of effective rank alone
failureModes: functional bank too easy or too hard

lenses.name: Selection-intensity-matched drift twin
lenses.rationale: Separates selection content from mere selection intensity for every world.
lenses.transformation: rerun with fitness values permuted among individuals each generation
observables: same observables as target lens under permuted fitness
failureModes: mutation bias alone produces the signal
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: Controls for selection intensity and mutation bias.

experiments.hypothesis: Sedimenting learned readouts into offspring reservoirs makes an abandoned ancestral task cheaper to relearn than a norm-matched random deposit does.
experiments.mechanism: Sedimentation operator W <- W + eps * v w_parent^T at each birth (eps=0.05, v random unit input-like vector), then rescale to keep rho unchanged.
experiments.intervention: Task A (delay-5 recall of u) for generations 0-40, task B (NARMA-5) for 41-80; at gen 80 measure few-shot (n=20 samples) readout NRMSE on task A.
experiments.control: Same run with no deposit operator (plain Gaussian weight mutation only).
experiments.positive_control: Insert the ridge-optimal task A readout (computed with n=2000) as the deposit at gen 80 directly; must reduce few-shot A error, otherwise the deposit channel cannot carry task content.
experiments.observable: Few-shot task A NRMSE at gen 80, mean over population elites, 10 seeds.
experiments.success_criterion: Sediment arm mean NRMSE_A <= 0.85 x null-twin mean, one-sided Mann-Whitney p < 0.05 over 10 seeds, AND positive control reduces NRMSE_A by >= 15%.
experiments.failure_criterion: Ratio > 0.95 or p >= 0.2, or positive control fails (then world is uninformative, not negative).
experiments.alternative_explanation: Deposits change the memory spectrum in a way that happens to favour delay recall regardless of content.
experiments.null_twin: Deposit W <- W + eps * v r^T with r random, ||r|| = ||w_parent||, same eps, same rho rescale: matches perturbation magnitude, rank and spectral effect, destroys content.
experiments.why_this_implementation: An ESN is the literal object of the Reservoir Computing concept, not a default ML ontology; population with rank-one deposits is the minimal form of sedimentation. Displaced alternative: a gradient-trained RNN, which would erase the fixed/active split.
experiments.size: population 30, leaky tanh ESN, N=50, sparse (10%), input dim 1, ridge readout lambda=1e-4, 300 steps + 50 washout, 80 generations, 10 seeds per arm, 3 arms (sediment, null twin, control)
experiments.cost_estimate: about 3 CPU core-minutes (30*80*10*3 = 72k evaluations at ~2 ms)
stupid_explanations: deposits increase rho before rescaling and rescaling is imperfect
task A and task B share delay structure so B-training preserves A
20-sample ridge is so noisy that any change in state scale shifts NRMSE
elites selected on B happen to carry A by chance at one seed

experiments.hypothesis: Selecting reservoirs for the number of decodable random functionals transfers to held-out functionals better than selecting for one task or for effective rank.
experiments.mechanism: Fitness = count of 20 training functionals decoded with R^2 > 0.5.
experiments.intervention: Four arms: richness selection, single-task selection (delay-5 recall), effective-rank selection, permuted-fitness twin.
experiments.control: Unevolved random reservoirs with matched rho and leak.
experiments.positive_control: Directly select on the held-out bank; must exceed control, bounding the attainable gain.
experiments.observable: Mean R^2 over 20 held-out functionals (random degree-2 polynomials of last 10 inputs).
experiments.success_criterion: Richness arm held-out mean R^2 exceeds single-task arm and effective-rank arm each by >= 0.05, over 8 seeds, paired by seed, sign test 7/8 or better.
experiments.failure_criterion: Richness minus effective-rank difference < 0.02 or sign test worse than 6/8.
experiments.alternative_explanation: Richness selection is just effective-rank selection with extra steps.
experiments.null_twin: Richness fitness values permuted among individuals each generation: matched selection intensity and mutation, destroyed link to decodability.
experiments.why_this_implementation: Linear decodability is the defining test of reservoir content; population search over fixed weights keeps the reservoir unlearned in life. Displaced: meta-learned neural representation.
experiments.size: population 24, leaky tanh ESN N=40, 50 generations, 8 seeds, 5 arms
experiments.cost_estimate: about 8 CPU core-minutes (20 ridge fits per evaluation, 24*50*8*5 evaluations)
stupid_explanations: held-out and training functionals share low-order terms
effective-rank arm poorly tuned so richness wins by default

experiments.hypothesis: Bracketing of distractor channels evolves when the readout budget is small but not when it is large.
experiments.mechanism: Heritable input mask over 8 channels (2 informative, 6 high-variance distractors); readout restricted to k taps.
experiments.positive_control: Hand-set mask excluding distractors: must beat all-ones at k=3 by >= 10% NRMSE, confirming bracketing is useful there.
experiments.observable: Fraction of distractor channels masked in elite genomes at gen 60.
experiments.success_criterion: Masked fraction >= 0.8 at k=3 and <= 0.4 at k=50, over 8 seeds (mean), and k=3 fraction exceeds permuted-fitness twin by >= 0.3.
experiments.failure_criterion: Difference between k=3 and k=50 masked fractions < 0.2.
experiments.alternative_explanation: Masking is selected wherever distractors add noise, independent of readout budget.
experiments.null_twin: Same k and channels, fitness permuted among individuals each generation.
experiments.why_this_implementation: The mask is a heritable gate before a fixed reservoir, the smallest bracketing that keeps channels in the world. Displaced: learned attention weights.
experiments.size: population 30, ESN N=50, 8 input channels, 60 generations, 8 seeds, 2 k values plus twin
stupid_explanations: at k=50 ridge already ignores distractors so there is no pressure
distractor variance saturates tanh, making masking a gain control

experiments.hypothesis: Evolved memory-capacity centroid tracks environmental delay, and a slow context period beyond the horizon is carried by the reservoir, not the readout.
experiments.mechanism: Heritable (rho, leak, weights); fitness = readout error on delayed recall with delay D in {2, 8, 20} plus a context bit that flips every 200 steps.
experiments.intervention: Vary D across environments; ablate readout vs reservoir at end (L2).
experiments.control: Random search over (rho, leak) with the same number of evaluations.
experiments.positive_control: Hand-set leak = 1/D; must shift MC centroid toward D.
experiments.observable: MC centroid lag (L1) and reservoir-attributed gain for the context bit (L2).
experiments.success_criterion: Spearman(D, centroid) >= 0.8 pooled over 3 D x 5 seeds, evolved beats random search NRMSE by >= 10%; context-bit gain from reservoir >= 0.1 NRMSE and from readout reset < 0.03.
experiments.failure_criterion: Evolved not better than random search by 5% (then M1 is just search) or context-bit gain < 0.03.
experiments.alternative_explanation: Any hyperparameter optimizer produces the tracking; context carried by trivial bias drift.
experiments.null_twin: Permuted-fitness evolution with identical mutation schedule.
experiments.why_this_implementation: Horizon is a property of the fixed dynamics, so only evolutionary change of the reservoir tests it. Displaced: backprop through time on a gated RNN.
experiments.size: population 20, ESN N=50, 40 generations, 3 D x 5 seeds, 3 arms, 2000-step runs
stupid_explanations: random search and evolution differ only in evaluation count bookkeeping
context bit leaks into input scaling
centroid defined poorly for flat profiles
